# KL2007 `docker-socket-mount`

A volume mounts the container runtime socket of the node.

Category: `security`. Severity: `error`. Enabled by default.

## What it does

Reports a `hostPath` volume that mounts a container runtime socket: a path whose file
name is `docker.sock`, `cri-dockerd.sock`, `containerd.sock`, `crio.sock` or
`podman.sock`, in a Pod and in the pod template of every workload kind. KL2005
`host-path-volume` does not report these volumes again.

Mounting a directory that holds a socket (such as `/var/run`) is reported by KL2005
only.

## Why it matters

The runtime socket is the API that starts containers on the node. Whoever can write to
it can start a privileged container that mounts the node's root filesystem, without
any Kubernetes check: no admission control, no Pod Security Standard, no audit log
entry for the new container. A mounted socket is root on the node.

The usual reason is building images inside the cluster ("Docker in Docker"). Builders
that need no daemon do this without the socket. Monitoring agents that read container
metadata can usually use the kubelet API instead. If an agent really needs the socket,
silence the finding for that object and say why.

## Example

```yaml
containers:
- name: build
  image: docker:27
  volumeMounts:
  - {name: docker, mountPath: /var/run/docker.sock}
volumes:
- name: docker
  hostPath:
    path: /var/run/docker.sock
```

Use instead:

```yaml
containers:
- name: build
  image: moby/buildkit:v0.17.0-rootless
```
